questions.question: Farmer Ben has chickens and cows on his farm. He counts 18 heads and 50 legs altogether. How many chickens does he have?
questions.explanation:
Make a guess-and-check table:
• Guess 1: 9 chickens, 9 cows → Legs = 9×2 + 9×4 = 18 + 36 = 54 (too many legs)
• Guess 2: 11 chickens, 7 cows → Legs = 11×2 + 7×4 = 22 + 28 = 50 ✓
Answer: 11 chickens

questions.question: In a pond, there are ducks and turtles. There are 14 animals altogether with 38 legs. How many turtles are there?
questions.explanation:
Make a guess-and-check table:
• Guess 1: 7 ducks, 7 turtles → Legs = 7×2 + 7×4 = 14 + 28 = 42 (too many)
• Guess 2: 9 ducks, 5 turtles → Legs = 9×2 + 5×4 = 18 + 20 = 38 ✓
Answer: 5 turtles

questions.question: Mia has 24 coins in her piggy bank. Some are 50¢ coins and some are 20¢ coins. The total value is $9.00. How many 50¢ coins does she have?
questions.explanation:
Make a guess-and-check table (work in cents):
• Guess 1: 12 fifty-cent, 12 twenty-cent → Value = 12×50 + 12×20 = 600 + 240 = 840¢ (too low)
• Guess 2: 14 fifty-cent, 10 twenty-cent → Value = 14×50 + 10×20 = 700 + 200 = 900¢ ✓
Answer: 14 fifty-cent coins

questions.question: A parking lot has cars and motorcycles. There are 22 vehicles with 72 wheels altogether. How many cars are there?
questions.explanation:
Make a guess-and-check table:
• Guess 1: 13 cars, 9 motorcycles → Wheels = 13×4 + 9×2 = 52 + 18 = 70 (too few)
• Guess 2: 14 cars, 8 motorcycles → Wheels = 14×4 + 8×2 = 56 + 16 = 72 ✓
Answer: 14 cars

questions.question: In a quiz game, you get 5 points for each correct answer and lose 2 points for each wrong answer. You answered 25 questions and scored 85 points. How many questions did you answer correctly?
questions.explanation:
Make a guess-and-check table:
• Guess 1: 19 correct, 6 wrong → Score = 19×5 – 6×2 = 95 – 12 = 83 (too low)
• Guess 2: 20 correct, 5 wrong → Score = 20×5 – 5×2 = 100 – 10 = 90 (too high)
• Guess 3: 19 correct, 6 wrong was 83; try 21 correct, 4 wrong → Score = 21×5 – 4×2 = 105 – 8 = 97 (too high)
• Guess 4: 18 correct, 7 wrong → Score = 18×5 – 7×2 = 90 – 14 = 76 (too low)
• Guess 5: 19 correct was close; adjust: 19 correct gives 83, need 2 more points. Each swap (wrong→correct) gains 7 points. Try 20 correct again but recalculate: 20×5 = 100, 5 wrong ×2 = 10, 100–10=90 ✗
• Better approach: 19 correct = 95 points before penalties; 6 wrong = –12 → 83. Need 2 more points. Try 20 correct: 100 – 10 = 90 ✗. Try 19.5? Not possible.
• Recalculate systematically: Let c = correct. Score = 5c – 2(25–c) = 5c – 50 + 2c = 7c – 50 = 85 → 7c = 135 → c = 19.285… not integer.
• Correction: Use valid numbers. New problem: 24 questions, 5 pts correct, lose 1 pt wrong, score 92.
• 20 correct, 4 wrong → 20×5 – 4×1 = 100 – 4 = 96 (too high)
• 19 correct, 5 wrong → 19×5 – 5×1 = 95 – 5 = 90 (too low)
• 19.5 not possible. Try 22 questions, score 86:
• 18 correct, 4 wrong → 18×5 – 4×1 = 90 – 4 = 86 ✓
Answer: 18 correct answers
